A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSR research work. Their complete main texts, supplementary sections, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable matching despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PSRBench and DreamBench evaluations, positional-encoding ablations, and qualitative metric comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline evaluations, a human user study, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The data-generation pipeline, frame-wise positional encoding, SFT/GRPO training, and combined subject-consistency, semantic, and aesthetic rewards remain unchanged. Figure 5 tests a PSR-only ablation of the existing reward design.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the approximately 350K-sample training corpus, seven PSRBench subsets, and DreamBench evaluation. The new human ratings and qualitative cases concern the existing generation task; no distinct dataset or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated MS-Diffusion and MOSAIC comparisons across PSRBench in Table 6. MS-Diffusion was previously cited but not evaluated. Existing comparator membership in Tables 1–5 remains unchanged; the new user study uses three previously evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: Section 10 introduces a limited human-evaluation protocol: five participants rank four methods on 100 randomly sampled test cases, assigning scores of 1, 0.8, 0.6, and 0.4. Existing benchmark protocols, training settings, and the positional-encoding ablation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 5 adds a qualitative PSR-only versus multi-reward comparison, an interaction example, a small-subject failure case, and a dataset category-frequency plot. These extend the analyses with illustrative evidence; the original positional-encoding ablation and metric-comparison cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added user-study and baseline tables report point scores without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Table 6 adds baseline scores: PSR leads overall, but MOSAIC exceeds it on Action aesthetic preference (0.933 versus 0.881) and Complex semantic alignment (0.818 versus 0.692). Table 7 adds human scores, with PSR leading at 0.92 SC, 0.80 SA, and 0.82 HPS. Figure 5 adds qualitative and dataset-distribution findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the associated mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same data pipeline, positional encoding, reward framework, benchmark, and effectiveness claims. The shortened conclusion preserves their substance; new supplementary evidence supports existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies difficulty preserving small-subject identity, interprets an interaction example as evidence against simple subject stacking, and describes the category distribution as relatively balanced. The explanation that multiple rewards mitigate copy-paste behavior already appears in v1.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including learning rates, LoRA ranks, GRPO group size, reward weights, image resizing, prompt templates, data filtering, and the code link. The added human-evaluation procedure is covered under E3.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references, including MOSAIC, ImagPose, and work on face/video generation, while retaining all earlier references. It also shortens the UNO discussion and removes the sentence describing OmniGen2's video-derived training data. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited affiliation/contact edits, condenses related-work prose and the conclusion, and adds three supplementary sections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–7 and the four-panel Figure 5, shortens Figure 2's caption, and reflows the document. Earlier figures remain intact, with supplementary Figures 5–10 renumbered 6–11; existing table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through two additional competitors and direct human judgments, while Figure 5 makes a concrete failure condition visible. These additions improve validation and transparency without changing the established method or results. The gain is limited because the user study has five participants without uncertainty estimates, and the reward and failure analyses remain illustrative rather than systematic.
